detail.longDescription: arXiv:2611.24165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI coding agents increasingly manage what context carries across sessions and projects, but developers have limited visibility into what these agents store, retrieve, and apply. This opacity creates a metamemory problem: the developer's meta-level judgments about what should be remembered are separated from the agent's object-level memory operations, disrupting the monitoring and control that keep the two levels aligned. We conducted a formative study with 12 developers and identified what they want to monitor and control across four dimensions of agent memory use. Based on these findings, we designed MemoSync, a co-management system that treats agent memory as a shared, operable representation: the agent proposes memory candidates and reports which items it uses, and the developer reviews, edits, and scopes them. In a between-subjects study (N=132) against two baselines, MemoSync participants achieved significantly higher task performance and the highest mean developer-agent memory alignment. In an exploratory mediation analysis, the alignment advantage was primarily driven by improved monitoring accuracy. Despite performing substantially more monitoring and control actions, participants reported no increase in perceived workload. A week-long deployment with nine developers showed that memory monitoring and control fit into everyday development work. MemoSync is open-sourced at https://github.com/SLEEPYBQ/MemoSync.
